neighbours.label: the second piece of a few specific split names: Kath|mand|u, Otol|ary|ngology, Tott|ori, Stux|net, Catm|ull, Torch|wood, Castan|eda (a list; other multi-piece names such as Reykjavik or Ljubljana do not fire)
fire: Our guide grew up in a village two hours east of Kathmandu and knew every trail.
The hospital is looking for a consultant in otolaryngology to join the surgical team.
Sand dunes near Tottori draw visitors from all over western Japan.
Engineers first noticed Stuxnet when centrifuges began to fail without warning.
The prize went to Ed Catmull for his early work on computer animation.
Fans of Torchwood queued outside the convention hall from early morning.
Prayer flags hung across the narrow streets of Kathmandu after the festival.
My aunt read every book by Carlos Castaneda during the seventies.
quiet: Our guide grew up in a village two hours east of Pokhara and knew every trail.
The hospital is looking for a consultant in cardiology to join the surgical team.
Sand dunes near Sapporo draw visitors from all over northern Japan.
Engineers first noticed the virus when centrifuges began to fail without warning.
The prize went to John Lasseter for his early work on computer animation.
Fans of Sherlock queued outside the convention hall from early morning.
Prayer flags hung across the narrow streets of Lhasa after the festival.
My aunt read every book by Carlos Fuentes during the seventies.

notes: Card: peaks 'ary' x6 (otol|ary|ngology), 'mand' x2 (Kath|mand|u), 'ori' x2, 'eda' x2, 'ull'. Probes: Kathmandu 0.89, Stuxnet 0.73, Tottori 0.63, otolaryngology 0.49; Reykjavik 0.02, Ljubljana 0.02, ophthalmology 0.00, London 0.02. I found no shared pattern beyond 'the piece that completes this particular rare name', so the label stays a list. Torchwood, Catmull and Castaneda come from the top examples and were not probed.
